start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-my-search-index-beside-a-copy-of-my-results with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and operations [{\"op\": \"save\", \"id\": \"r1\", \"text\": \"bakery bread sourdough\"}, {\"op\": \"index_page\", \"limit\": 10}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the results and the index are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-my-search-index-beside-a-copy-of-my-results" with store and the operations to run. Ask the person first about what to save or delete.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the saves and deletes through those objects, and pages the index by its own cursor; a search reads the index as it is.

worked_examples.title: A bakery result saved, then indexed and searched
worked_examples.ask: Save the result r1 with the text bakery bread sourdough, then index the changes and search for bakery.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the index kept in the store's own objects, made by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: answers ["saved", {"indexed": ["r1"], "more": false}, ["r1"]] and found_results ["r1"] with r1 indexed.
